characters.name: Alicia Florrick (née Cavanaugh)
characters.description: The title character and main protagonist.A graduate of Georgetown University Law Center,Alicia worked as a litigator for a couple of years, but then married Peter Florrick and spent the next fifteen years as a housewife. After Peter is involved in a public sex scandal and faces the threat of prison, she goes back to her former career to support herself and their children. But, having been away from the job so long, she has to start as a junior and make her way up the ladder from scratch. The Alcoholic: While she was never exactly a teetotaler, she develops a mild drinking problem in season 7 fromthe accumulated misery of the past six years. Oddly, she finds she drinks less after starting her affair with Jason Crouse. Aloof Dark-Haired Girl: She's generally cool and composed, especially when she's in court, with dark brown hair. She also gradually becomes more aloof over time. Amoral Attorney: Alicia has a strong sense of professional ethics, but the law is her job and she will still do whatever she can within the confines of the law to advocate for her client, regardless of their guilt or innocence. She represents murderers like Colin Sweeney and drug kingpin Lemond Bishop just as readily as she does genuinely innocent people, but isn't afraid to make her personal distaste for less-reputable clients known (she considers Sweeney a creep and is subtly terrified of Bishop). Beware the Nice Ones: She's usually nice and calm, but when she gets angry, look out. Threatening her family is an especially dumbass move. It has only increased sincedeparting Lockhart-Gardner.Alicia:[sweetly] Die choking on your own blood.

characters.name: Zach Florrick
characters.description: Alicia and Peter's older child, their son. All Girls Want Bad Boys:Gender-Inverted: he has a tendency especially withManipulative BitchBecca, who is older than him. Big Brother Instinct: Throughout. He viciously beats up a friend upon discovering he's been creeping on Grace, and is constantly protective of his mom. Dating What Mommy Hates: Alicia hates Becca and is concerned about almost all of Zach's girlfriends, especially after college when heelopes to France and marries his latest girlfriend. That said, she does her best to simply offer counsel and then respect his choices, and she takes umbrage when anybody outside the family tries to interfere in his love life. Momma's Boy: Very downplayed, but Alicia and Zach are close and it's portrayed very positively.

characters.name: Grace Florrick
characters.description: Alicia and Peter's younger child, their daughter. "All Grown Up" Remark: Played for drama after Season 2 and more into 3 as Grace grows up and becomes the object of creepy websites and pictures on the Internet. Annoying Younger Sibling: Downplayed. Grace is pretty mature and tries her best, but she still sometimes annoys Zach as he needs to be protective towards her. In the Blood: She grows to admire her mother's renewed legal career and decides to go to law school herself in the final season, and interns at Florrick & Quinn as their secretary for several episodes. Plucky Office Girl: Having been aPlucky Girlthroughout most of the series, she becomes one of these when she steps up to help Alicia in law and managing house in Season 6.

characters.name: Peter Florrick
characters.description: Alicia's estranged husband and former Illinois State's Attorney for Cook County, who became embroiled in a major sex and corruption scandal thattriggered the plot of the series. 10-Minute Retirement: Apparently from politics at the beginning of Season 1 when he goes to prison, but it (predictably) doesn't stick. The Atoner: He's ostensibly trying to make up for what he did both as a political figure and as a husband;however, it gradually becomes apparent that he's more interested inlookinglike he's changed than in actually changing. Betty and Veronica: Deconstructed between him and Will. Will should be the Betty, as Peter cheated on Alicia and got her involved in some shady dealings, but Peter is much more Betty-like in that Alicia comes to see him as the safe option as their family can be together. Fake Guest Star: Despite his importance throughout the series as the husband of the titular good wife, Chris Noth was only ever billed as part of the recurring cast.

characters.name: Jackie Florrick
characters.description: Alicia's overbearing and antagonistic mother-in-law. December–December Romance: She happens to meet Howard Lyman in the final season. They fall inLove at First Sightand marry in the second-to-last episode. Freudian Excuse: For all the mayhem she causes Alicia, it's suggested thather mother was abusive: Jackie recalls to Howard that her mother hated what her laughter sounded like and made her eat a clove of garlic every time she laughed. Hypocrite: She despises even the mere thought that Alicia might leave Peter over his infidelity, but we learn eventually that her own late husband was no more faithful than her son: she tries to derail the nomination of a woman to the Illinois Supreme Court for having been the elder Mr. Florrick's mistress many years ago. My Beloved Smother: Both Peter and Alicia find her attempts to meddle in their personal lives annoying, and half of Eli's job as Peter's campaign manager and chief of staff is corralling her some days.

characters.name: Owen Cavanaugh
characters.description: Alicia's younger brother and Peter Florrick's brother-in-law. A professor of mathematics, he moves to the University of Chicago in season 2. Big Sister Worship: He loves and admires Alicia and geninuely wants her to be happy in both her personal and professional lives, and once threatens to kill Peter if he ever cheats on her again. Camp Gay:Downplayed. He's openly gay and has a stereotypical "gay guy" voice, but otherwise doesn't flaunt it very much. Shipper on Deck: He's deeply in favor of Alicia making a fresh start romantically with some newTall, Dark, and Handsomeparamour, particularly Will Gardner.

characters.name: Veronica Loy
characters.description: Alicia and Owen's mother and Peter Florrick's mother-in-law, a mercurial, chaotic soul who has married, divorced, and outlived multiple men. Bumbling Dad:Gender-Inverted. Alicia and Owen love her but aren't afraid to critique her spending and romance habits and mercurial and flighty personality. Hard-Drinking Party Girl: She's a wild soul at heart and is hardly ever seen without some kind of booze in hand. Odd Friendship: She becomes one of the mercenary and antisocial David Lee's only actual friends over the course of the series after he represents her in an estate dispute with her stepson. Shipper on Deck: Like her son, she frequently encourages Alicia to move on from Peter, particularly while Will is in the picture.

characters.name: Diane Lockhart
characters.description: One of the three named partners of what is initially called Stern, Lockhart & Gardner, and a staunch liberal feminist activist often known forcaring more about the cause than the payout. Being Good Sucks: Numerous times her liberal values are put in direct contrast with her work, or they're straight-up tested as when she learns that her father betrayed his best friend and was not the best of people. Character Development: Overlapping withEarly-Installment Weirdness. In the pilot, Christine Baranski played Diane as considerably more loud, gregarious and brusque compared to her more stoic characterisation in future episodes. The Gadfly: She sometimes trolls herLove InterestKurtMcVeighby randomly name-dropping left-wing talking points, just to watch him twitch. Informed Attribute: Played with. In the early seasons, her supposed extremely close friendship with Will consists of a few scenes of them joking together (and slow-dancing, on one occasion), while they spend most of their time at odds over one thing or another. This changes considerably starting in season 3, when Will's past misdeeds come to light and Diane stands by him without question regardless of the consequences for herself, revealing the depth of their bond and their loyalty to one another.

characters.name: Will Gardner
characters.description: The other managing partner of Lockhart/Gardner and the partner who decided to take a chance on hiring Alicia after Peter's scandal, thanks in part to their ambiguous but important past friendship from law school. Ambiguous Situation: Played for Drama in the episode "The Last Call."Alicia spends the entire episode speculating what Will's final message on the phone was about. Was he calling to make peace with her? Was he calling to tell her to stop poaching his clients? Was there another reason? By the end of the episode, Alicia comes to accept she'll never know the truth since Will is dead. Amoral Attorney: Was one in the past, and still displays some signs, such as when he tries to blackmail a judge (while being investigated for potentiallybribingjudges). He's largely balanced out by the more moral Diane and Alicia, though both fail him at times. Back for the Finale:Despite being dead, he briefly appears in anImagine Spotby Alicia in the series finale. Badass Bookworm: A brilliant lawyer who is also physically endowed and totally willing to fight when he needs to.

characters.name: Kalinda Sharma
characters.description: A crack investigator with Lockhart/Gardner. Action Girl: On a show full of lawyers (hencelotsof talking), Kalinda acts rather than chats. Aloof Dark-Haired Girl: She's an attractive brunette in an imposing way and has an aloof demeanour. Ax-Crazy: She can come across as this when pushed too far, because she will do exactly what it takes, including illegal and immoral actions, to get shady people what they deserve. Beware the Quiet Ones: Kalinda is a woman of few words, but she is the last person you want to go up against.

characters.name: Cary Agos
characters.description: Began the series as an associate at Lockhart/Gardner with Alicia, competing for one permanent slot. Eventually bounces around until finally striking out for professional independence. Break the Haughty: His stay in prison during Season 6 becomes this for him. He's much softer after that. Butt-Monkey: Cary is very smug, but it's hard not to sympathise with him because of how often he loses: the position to Alicia in Season 1, respect in Season 2 at the State's Attorney, his job at Lockhart-Gardner once again. The Casanova: He really gets around and is popular with most of the young women that Lockhart-Gardner encounters. Chronic Backstabbing Disorder: Hasn't had a boss yet who he hasn't turned on at some point.Includinghimself, in a sense, when he went behind Alicia's back at Florrick-Agos.

characters.name: David Lee
characters.description: Head of Family Law at Lockhart/Gardner, who is antagonistic as often as he's on the main characters' side. Ambiguously Gay: He is seemingly unmarried and is never shown taking a romantic interest in any other character. In "Undisclosed Recipients", a series of leaked emails at the firm shows that some employees suspect him of being gay, though he denies it. Amoral Attorney: He's out for himself (and to a lesser extenthis relatives) first and foremost, not his clients or the firm. He's been suspected of faking legal documents on at least one occasion. Deadpan Snarker: While everyone has their moments, David Lee takes the cake; he has a line for every single circumstance. Humanizing Tears: After hearing aboutWill's death, David Lee immediately storms out of the main boardroom, finds a conference room,orders everybody in the room out, and then bursts into a brief sob overthe death of his friend. It's probably the greatest indication in the entire show that Lockhart/Gardner'sToken Evil Teammatereally does have a heart.

characters.name: Glenn Childs
characters.description: Peter's successor as Illinois State Attorney. Amoral Attorney: He's extremely corrupt and went as far to frame Peter for his corruption. And he's an attorney, although not a practicing one. Corrupt Politician: And how, shown by his deep involvement in illegal business practices. Put on a Bus: He disappears from the series after the season 2 finale, having lost his reelection bid. The Rival: To Peter Florrick, partly because he's his replacement in his job, and then later when Peter challenges him for the position.

characters.name: Matan Brody
characters.description: A recurring Assistant State's Attorney for Cook County whose main role in the series is torepeatedly lose to the protagonists. Black Gal on White Guy Drama: He tries to gin some up with Dana Lodge overCary's "type" being brown-skinned women, though he fails as miserably at that as at everything else. Butt-Monkey: His entire role is basically to be aJerkasswho is repeatedly humiliated by every other lawyer he encounters. He almost never wins a single case on-screen literally from the pilot episode until "KSR" in the last season (andthatconviction gets tossed on the merits by Judge Schakowsky), and even routinely gets upstaged by fellow A.S.A.s. Smug Snake: He's a near-constantly grinning smarmyJerkasswho is always overconfident about his chances in court.

characters.name: Eli Gold
characters.description: A fixer employed by Peter Florrick to deal with the fallout from his sex scandal. Later his campaign manager and chief of staff. The Ace: He's known for being the best, and he brings a lot of money to the firm when he joins in Season 3, although it borders onInformed Attributewith all the mistakes he makes. Berserk Button: "I hate AMATEURS!" Don't do anything to hurt Eli's campaign if you don't want him to spit coffee and throw books or strangle you. Consummate Liar: A point of pride with him.Eli:Look, I lie 24/7 for my job. It's actually a gift. Culturally Religious: He's an ethnic Jew and Marissa once even tries to get him to move to Israel to work on the campaign of an anti-Likud political candidate. However, he's never indicated to actually practice Judaism as a religion.

characters.name: Colin Sweeney
characters.description: A recurring client of Lockhart/Gardner (and later Reddick, Boseman, and Lockhart). Sweeney is a finance CEO with a taste for kinky rough sex who relishes the notoriety from tabloid gossip around him, and was oncefound not guilty of murdering his first wife. Bondage Is Bad: Justified in that he's also a murderer, but his perverse, overtly sexual interests are very disturbing. Comedic Sociopathy: Sweeney's blasé attitude towards killing his wife and overall creepiness are usually played forBlack Comedy. Has a Type: He seems to prefer attractive, dark-haired, self-possessed women who are interested in unconventional sex/relationships. While most of those apply to Alicia — who hemaybe interested in — he also likes her as a lawyer and, he says, as a person. She’s also the closest thing he has to an actual friend, apparently. Hated by All: Sweeney's second wife, Isobel Swift, is the only person in the entire series who has any affection for him, and that's only because she's just as much of a sociopath as him. Otherwise, Sweeney is universally despised for killing his wife and getting away with it by the State's Attorney's office, the public, judges and even his own lawyers, who are consistently creeped out by his dark sense of humor and overtly sexual comments and frustrated by his being a horribly unreliable witness who they have to scramble to defend. One judge even outright calls Sweeney a scumbag to his face during a trial he's presiding over in which Sweeney is the defendant, admitting he's likely to be reprimanded for this but considering it to be worth it.

characters.name: Nancy Crozier
characters.description: A recurring attorney who hides her competence behind an act of being a naive small-town girl from Michigan. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: She acts sensitive and innocent, but she is no less ruthless than any other lawyer on the show. Dumb Blonde: She totally acts like she's one, but as Alicia learns the first time she goes toe-to-toe with her, she's extremely intelligent and sharp. It'sallan act. Manipulative Bitch: Is good at putting on an innocent act, and likes to exploit it. Obfuscating Stupidity: Minor example as she often claims her lack of knowledge to be from innocence, but she can veer towards it a great deal.

characters.name: KurtMcVeigh
characters.description: A renowned ballistics expert and member of the Tea Party, and Diane's mainLove Interestthroughout the franchise. Absence Makes the Heart Go Yonder:Implied. Season 7 reveals that in the three years he and Diane have been married, they've only seen each other 98 days.In the series finale, Lucca targets him on the stand with the revelation that he cheated on Diane at some point. The Ace: There is absolutely no question that Kurt is the best ballistics expert in the business. He isn't rightallthe time, but it's usually because he was missing a critical piece of information that would have altered his conclusions, rather than a simple error in analysis. Everybody Loves Blondes: He has a weakness for blondes, particularlyconservative ones. When he sells his business so he can move in with Diane in the last season, his buyer turns out to be one, and Diane and David Lee accuse her ofusing her looks to get him to agree to a lowballed price; he initially rejects this but later agrees to find another buyer. Everyone Has Standards:He's a bit of aGun Nut, being an outspoken advocate of the Second Amendment and having dedicated his career to the study of ballistics, but he will not stand for malfunctioning guns being allowed into general circulation.Kurt despises Colin Sweeney for killing his first wife and getting away with it, but agrees to help Lockhart & Gardner defend him from a trumped-up charge for dangerous gun use when his investigation reveals that Sweeney is, in fact,innocent of that crime.

characters.name: Lemond Bishop
characters.description: A Chicago drug lord who retains the services of Lockhart/Gardner for legal representation in cases relating to his legal(-ish) business and family matters. Affably Evil: Despite running a criminal gang and drug dealing operation, he is a charming, suave guy and a good parent. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: He is a genuinely loving, caring father to his son, Dylan. He tells Kalinda that his own fatherran out on him when he was six, and he is determined to be better with his own child. Knight Templar Parent: Subverted in one episode, when he learns that his son is being bullied at school. Kalinda becomes afraid that he will respond by going after the bully or his family,Bishop simply calls the bully's parents and, in a very reasonable manner, tells them what their son is doing and asks them to talk to him about it. Put on a Prison Bus:He's finally brought down for good at the end of season 6 when Kalinda steals files from his computer for Geneva Pine in exchange for not being charged with obstruction. He's quickly arrested, and the last we hear of him in the season finale, he's awaiting trial.

characters.name: Elsbeth Tascioni
characters.description: An eccentric but brilliant lawyer. For tropes related to her inElsbeth, gohere. Attention Deficit... Ooh, Shiny!: She can have trouble keeping a train of thought; in one episode when she goes up in court against Alicia, she uses this to throw Elsbeth off her game by leaving conspicuous magazines on her desk in the courtroom. Beware the Nice Ones: She is incredibly friendly and likable to just about anyone she meets, but may God have mercy on your soul if you go up against her in some legal action. Beware the Silly Ones: Though, she can be a bit of an oddball at times, but it is not wise to make her uspet.

characters.name: Judge Charles Abernathy
characters.description: A trial judge on the Circuit Court of Cook County, and one of the more frequent recurring judges with nine total appearances onThe Good Wifeplus three onThe Good Fight. Characterized as a bleeding-heart liberal, even by Diane's standards. Beware the Nice Ones: He's usually a softie and a bit of a pushover, and even dislikes using his gavel. In his final appearance in the last season, he himself pullsLoophole Abuseto allow a billboard accusing a gun dealer of culpability in a teenage girl's death to temporarily stay up even after he was forced to rule it defamatory,noteSpecifically, since it was a bench trial and therefore he got to decide damages, he set the fine at a 10 cents per day the billboard remained up, and then let thePapa Wolfdefendant pay up front with the $40 he had in his pocket.and tells the plaintiff to get used to the idea that actions have consequences. Establishing Character Moment: Pausing his trial before opening remarks in order to hold a moment of silence for the contemporary genocide in Darfur. Fox News Liberal: Played with: He's definitely a bleeding-heart, but he's actually somewhat unpredictable when cases get political, which Diane attributes to him tending to feel guilty about his own liberal bias and overcompensating.

characters.name: Wendy Scott-Carr
characters.description: Peter's opponent in the race for State Attorney in Season 2. Best Served Cold: She seems to just want to do her job properlyuntil she reveals to Will who she's really after in season 3, which she's been waiting for since Season 2. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: She has young children, she's very softly-spoken, and she's extremely ruthless and ambitious, as everyone who comes across her learns. Fake Boobs:Played for Drama: Eli tries to poke holes in her "woman of the people" image when he discovers she's had some work done, but it backfires horribly when she reveals in an interview that the implants were a concession to vanity after she had a double mastectomy due to breast cancer. Smug Snake: And how! She's always smiling regardless of whether she's being beaten or not.

characters.name: Louis Canning
characters.description: A rival lawyer to Lockhart/Gardner who suffers from tardive dyskinesia (a proxy for his actor's Parkinson's disease) and loves to milk his condition for jury sympathy in court. Affably Evil: Canning represents some very shady clients with zero remorse, but he's still a genuinely friendly guy who loves his wife and kids and has enormous respect for Alicia's skill in court. Amoral Attorney: Canning can usually be found defending pharmaceutical corporations from class actions for unsafe medicines they've produced, and resorts to extremely dirty tactics in court. Some of his stunts, like the time he acted asThe Molefor the defendant, should realistically have resulted in sanctions or disbarment, but he apparently hasJoker Immunity. Disability as an Excuse for Jerkassery: Canning constantly milks his tardive dyskinesia for sympathy from judges and juries, then acts offended or accuses his opponents of discriminating against him when called out on it. He finally meets his match when he tries it on a paraplegic judge in chambers, who tells him in no uncertain terms to knock it off and present his case. Kansas City Shuffle: He almost always has a second angle he's working behind his back. In his first appearance, he reveals after settling for $34 million that he thought the Case of the Week was worth three times that, and he wasactuallyhired to reduce the payout rather than prevent it altogether.He also helps force Lockhart-Gardner into bankruptcy and then tries to buy the firm himself, by collaborating with Patty Nyholm to sue the firm so that he can steal some of their top clients while they're distracted.

characters.name: Marissa Gold
characters.description: Eli's daughter. Had a recurring role inThe Good Wifeand later became a regular onThe Good Fight, where she works as Diane's assistant at Reddick, Boseman & Kolstad and later as an investigator at the same firm. Ascended Extra: She first appears as a fleeting guest star, but she gets a permanent position as Alicia's assistant due to their association with Eli, and then she becomes a permanent main cast member on the spinoff. Crouching Moron, Hidden Badass: She puts on the demeanor of a jokeyWomanchildand constantly annoys her father. She's also very intelligent and observant, and is an Israeli army veteran on top of it (although we don't whether she ever saw combat). Hyper-Competent Sidekick: This is actually why she becomes an assistant (to Alicia) in Season 6 at all. Deadpan Snarker: Like her father, she's extremely witty and intelligent.

characters.name: Neil Gross
characters.description: The wealthy CEO of Chumhum, an large Internet conglomerate. His role varies depending on the episode: early on he's usually a defendant, later on he becomes a client. Corrupt Corporate Executive: He helped the Chinese government track down dissidents in exchange for getting to do business there, and manipulated his search algorithm to bury competing companies (and to make "disbarred lawyer" appear after every search for Will Gardner's name, which isPlayed for Laughs). No Celebrities Were Harmed: He's presented as a bit of aComposite Characterof Google co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin and Facebook founder Mark Zuckerberg: he's aNouveau Riche,Ambiguously Jewish(Zuckerberg) tech CEO with a reputation for ruthlessness and playing fast and loose with the law. Starter Marriage: Lockhart & Gardner helps him and his wife negotiate a prenup. Based on how nasty that turned out, it's little surprise when they divorce within a year.

characters.name: Howard Lyman
characters.description: A legacy partner at Lockhart/Gardner brought back to the firm by Will and Diane to help them vote Bond out of the firm in Season 2. He remains at the firm for the rest of the series, and causes a lot of trouble due to his senility and lack of political correctness. Chivalrous Pervert: Despite (or perhaps because of) hisDirty Old Mantendencies, he's surprisingly favorable towards hiring women to work at the firm, even siding with Diane on Monica Timmons in season 7. December–December Romance: He gets engaged to Jackie Florrick in Season 7. Dirty Old Man: He nearly brings a sexual harassment suit down on the firm by making a pass at a paralegal and ruins a simple meeting with Latina client Natalie Flores because he can't resist going off on a tangent about how sexy Mexican women are. Informed Judaism: He mentions he's Jewish briefly in the middle of the series. The only other time it comes up is when he marries Jackie in a ketubah-signing ceremony (a traditional marriage contract in Judaism).

characters.name: Burl Preston
characters.description: A recurring lawyer for media companies who first appears in "Net Worth". Consummate Professional: He's always impeccably dressed and seems to dislikeCourtroom Anticsand getting into shouting matches, preferring to present arguments in a calm and matter-of-fact manner. Enemy Mine: He reluctantly teams up with Will Gardner to battle Florrick/Agos in "Goliath and David" over a plagiarism case. Omnidisciplinary Lawyer: He does specialize in working for media companies, but in his four appearances on the show, he handled defamation, two tort cases, and a copyright suit. Punch-Clock Villain: He's an antagonist but not a bad guy. In "Anatomy of a Joke" he even offers to drop his case against Therese Dodd if she helps his client lobby the FCC not to fine them, since he knows she can't possibly afford the judgement.

characters.name: Colonel Leora Kuhn
characters.description: A Colonel in the US Army Judge Advocate General's Corps who presides over criminal cases involving Chicago area Army personnel. Appeared in three episodes ofThe Good Wifeand one ofThe Good Fight. Consummate Professional: She's anIron Ladywhether behind the bench or in front of it and doesn't appreciateCourtroom Antics.Exploitedby Will when he stages a disrespectful outburst in court and she has him arrested on contempt charges, letting Alicia invoke a trial rule that forces her to grant the defense team a continuance due to her having to take over as first chair. Iron Lady: She's a stoic, no-nonsense middle-aged Army officer. A Mother to Her Men: Her last appearance in the series has her take up a rape accusation by a younger female JAG officer, Laura Hellinger, when the Army declined to press charges, and hands it to Alicia to try for someJustice by Other Legal Meansin civil court.

characters.name: Mike Kresteva
characters.description: A lawyer and influential figure in Politics; he runs as the Republican candidate for Governor against Peter Florrick. Gaslighting: In pretty much every appearance, he will conduct a conversation with someone, then later claim to their faces that they said things they did not say. His insistence that his fiction is fact, and his condescending attitude towards his victims' attempts to correct him, makes him truly despicable. Hoist by His Own Petard: Peter turns hisGaslightingtricks against him by punching him in the face and then brazenly lying about it, telling everyone Kresteva got too drunk and fell in the bathroom. Jerk with a Heart of Jerk: Every time he shows even the slightest hint of a sympathetic trait, it will either turn out to be an act or will be something that he exploits for his own gain. Recovered Addict: He's mentioned to be a recovering alcoholic, and steadfastly avoids booze.Exploitedby Peter in "Death of a Client" to get back at him for his latest lie about the Florrick family: he bloodies Kresteva's nose then makes it look like he was sneaking a drink in the bathroom and slipped.

characters.name: Clarke Hayden
characters.description: A trustee appointed to manage the firm's finances during season 4. Badass Bureaucrat: You know you're doing something right if you make David Lee sweat during a negotiation. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: His last appearance was in the season 5 episode "A Weird Year". After that, like many people who worked atAlicia and Cary's law firm, he then just disappeared from the story and was never again mentioned, not reappearing until season 2 ofElsbeth. Consummate Professional: He is a firmly no-nonsense accountant and lawyer who takes any job he's given extremely seriously. When he's appointed as trustee to get the firm out of bankruptcy, he frequently butts heads with Will and Diane because of it, but he also protects the firm from a hostile takeover attempt by Louis Canning in large part becausehe didn't appreciate Canning's attempt to buy him with a job offer.When he applies to Florrick-Agos, he sweetens the deal by offering to defer his salary until they're solvent. Defrosting Ice King: Was fairly distant at first, but became much more personally invested with the firm over time; in "Waiting For The Knock", he even uncovered vital clues while assisting in a case.

characters.name: Judge Michael Marx
characters.description: An elderly Chicago judge who is nonetheless sharp as a tack. Cool Old Guy: Despite being quite elderlynotehis actor was 81 in his first appearancewith failing hearing, his intellect hasn't suffered one bit: in his first appearance, involving a lawsuit against Neil Gross's tech company Chumhum, he turns out to have a considerable amount of very technical knowledge on the functioning of search engines. He's also quick to clamp down onCourtroom Anticsfrom Will afterCary and Alicia split to start their own firm.

characters.name: Captain (ret.) Laura Hellinger
characters.description: A US Army JAG officer introduced to Alicia by Col. Kuhn after accusing another soldier of sexually assaulting her. Alicia later helps her get a job as an A.S.A. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: She disappears from the series with no further explanation after dumping Will at the end of "The Wheels of Justice". She alluded to reconnecting with aNew Old Flame, but there was no indication she was leaving town or her job for it. Dating Catwoman: She ends up casually dating Will for a bit despite being an A.S.A. who is frequently sitting across from him in court. Rape as Backstory: Her introductory episode has her suing another soldier for sexually assaulting her in Afghanistan. Screw This, I'm Outta Here: She resigns her commission after her sexual assault lawsuit isdismissed on a technicality, following the Army refusing to try her attacker.

characters.name: Charles Lester
characters.description: An associate of Lemond Bishop. Supposedly a consulting lawyer, he acts more as a fixer or an enforcer. Amoral Attorney: Though the "attorney" thing seems to be more of a cover for a less legal profession. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Despite his old, harmless exterior and overall amiable attitude, he is a ruthless and loyal operative working for an equally brutal drug lord. Obfuscating Stupidity: When he works with Alicia and talks to witnesses, he just asks irrelevant questions. However, he is sharper and more ruthless than that when issuing threats. The Pirates Who Don't Do Anything: As Alicia points out in his first appearance, in his 25 years as a lawyer, Lester has never tried a case, written a brief, been part of a firm or had an office and has only had two clients, namely Bishop and a mafia don who died ten years previously. This is because being a lawyer is just a cover for his real job, which is intimidating witnesses on Bishop's behalf.

characters.name: Robyn Burdine
characters.description: Lockhart/Gardner's second investigator, hired to work alongside Kalinda in Season 4. Beneath Suspicion: When Will finds out that Alicia is leaving to start her own firm with Cary, he assigns Robyn to keep track of Alicia's movements until he can have her fired and escorted out of the building. It's clear he never suspected that the cute, sweet Robyn was actually planning on joining Alicia's firm, and she immediately begins helping her new boss take client files with no one being any the wiser until Kalinda blows her cover. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: She disappears without a trace after the second episode of Season 6. Foil: She contrasts with Kalinda whenever they work together, being a bubbly blondeNice Girlto the dark-haired, distant, serious Kalinda. Nice Girl: She's cheerful and friendly with everyone.

characters.name: Josh Perotti
characters.description: A scheming U.S. Attorney who has a habit of playing fast and loose with defendants' rights and a massive crush on Elsbeth Tascioni. Abhorrent Admirer: He has a huge crush on Elsbeth, who normally finds him quite off-putting. Amoral Attorney: He has a habit of playing fast and loose with the Fourth and Fifth Amendments, including brazenly rewriting and even shredding documents indicating he broke the law in obtaining wiretaps, and railroading Eli by subpoenaing everyone he can think of to testify against him, up to and including Jackie Florrick. Did Not Get the Girl: He actually manages to seduce Elsbeth in his last appearance, but she catches him at yet more illegal shenanigans later and makes clear that will be the only time. Smug Snake: His default facial expression is a smarmy smirk, and he's completely unflappable in his efforts to get his man by any means he deems necessary.

characters.name: Carey Zepps
characters.description: A lawyer at Lockhart/Gardner who leaves with Alicia and Cary to join Florrick/Agos. One-Steve Limit: Averted and lampshaded. Several characters confuse him with Cary Agos and Neil Gross even suggests one of them change their name. Remember the New Guy?: He's never seen before Season 5, then shows up as one of the associates planning on leaving Lockhart/Gardner with Alicia and Cary as if he's been around all along, despite the fact that he very noticeably was not among this group during Cary's meetings with them in Season 4. Suddenly Bilingual: He's randomly revealed to speak fluent Russian, which comes in handy when Florrick, Agos & Lockhart suffers a ransomware attack by a Russian hacker: he's able to translate between Kalinda and the hacker while she blackmails him into decrypting their files.

characters.name: Finn Polmar
characters.description: An ASA who goes up against Will in court, only to find himself embedded in the politics and personal life of the main cast following a terrible tragedy. Amicable Exes: He's divorced but is on good terms with his ex. Towards the end of season 6 he mentions that they've started dating again. Died in Your Arms Tonight: Tries to stop the bleeding whenWill is shot; failing that, holds and tries to comforthimuntil help arrives. Incorruptible Pure Pureness: In a world full ofGrey-and-Gray Morality, even among the "good guys", Finn definitely has the straightest moral compass, shying away from his "hero" image following the shooting and evenquitting his ASA jobupon discovering Castro's true intentions. Nice Guy: Genuinely kind, charming, funny, and warm, particularly towards Alicia.

characters.name: Johnny Elfman
characters.description: An in-demand, blunt political advisor who becomes the campaign manager for a later State's Attorney race. The Cynic: Starts out utterly utilitarian and cynical when questioningAliciaabout motives for running, but gradually comes to truly believe inher.Alicia: How do you know that I can do better things than Prady?Johnny: Because I... I've talked with you, and been with you, and...I believe in you. Emotionally Tongue-Tied: Turns out that for all his quick thinking and strategic ruthlessness, when it comes to his feelings forAlicia, he turns into a stammering dork who can hardly meet her eyes. Foil: To Eli. Both are political advisers/consultants working witha Florrickon a campaign, but Eli is immensely snarky and hot-tempered, while John tends towards a calmer, more thoughtful demeanor. Manipulative Bastard: A job requirement, though to a much lesser degree than Eli.

characters.name: Frank Prady
characters.description: A CBS law journalist who runs against Alicia for State's Attorney in season 6. Ambiguously Gay: Even though he is divorced and has two children, there is a rumor that he is secretly gay.He's not. He hasn't remarried because he is a Jesuit, so for him a second marriage would be considered adultery. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome:He exits the series after conceding the election in "Red Meat", and doesn't even reappear while his proxies are fighting Alicia over election fraud allegations in "Winning Ugly". Incorruptible Pure Pureness: Frank borders on this when he's in the race with Alicia, which Alicia and Eli find very difficult to deal with as they're used to being more unscrupulous. He genuinely wants to make Chicago better, and Alicia collaborate to kill negative political ads against each other. Nice Guy: One of the most moral politicians featured on the show, especially in contrast to Glenn Childs, and he's always nice to Alicia.

characters.name: Guy Radmayne
characters.description: A rich, old Democratic mega-donor. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: When he and Alicia first meet, he comes off as a harmless old man, but quickly reveals a less pleasant side. Dirty Old Man:DoubleSubverted. When he is introduced, he appears next to a much younger woman in a photo. She turns out to be his granddaughter/assistant and not a trophy wife, as it might appear at first glance. However, when he meets Alicia alone, he gets pretty creepy. Another time, when he hugs her, she is disgusted by him pressing his groin up against her while doing so. Heteronormative Crusader: He doesn't want to back Frank Prady for district attorney because he is rumored to be a closeted gay man and Redmayne, in his own words, "[doesn't] like fags". Screw the Rules, I Have Money!: When Frank Prady calls him out for his unpleasant behavior:Frank:You... you're disgusting!Redmayne:Right, but I’m rich, so it really doesn’t matter, does it?

characters.name: Reese "R.D." Dipple
characters.description: The fourth-richest man in the United States, R.D. spends his billions on bankrolling conservative legal activism. An old acquaintance of KurtMcVeigh's, he's introduced when Kurt takes Diane on a hunting trip to make up for a case that put them at odds, and starts working with her on cases. Enemy Mine: R.D. notes when collaborating with Florrick, Agos & Lockhart on a legal challenge to mandatory minimum sentencing that fiscal conservatives like himself and liberals like Diane both agree that they're bad policy, even if they differ as to why: "Liberals think that mandatory minimums are draconian and unfair. We think they're wasteful and unfair." Fiction 500: He's said to be the fourth-richest man in the United States when introduced in a 2015 episode, whichaccording to Forbes' list that yearwould put him between Oracle founder Larry Ellison and Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos at a net worth of roughly $47 billion. According to Kurt, he has a much lower profile since his businesses are all old-school manufacturing companies: "gases, pulp, and paper". In-Series Nickname: He actively prefers the initialism "R.D." to his full name, though his proxy Ethan Carver refers to him as "Mr. Dipple". Put on a Bus: R.D. stops appearing in person after "The Deconstruction", instead acting through his house counsel Ethan Carver.Justifiedsince he does have an actual job besides beingUncle Pennybagsto conservative legal plaintiffs.

characters.name: Lucca Quinn
characters.description: A bar attorney with four years of experience who hits it off with Alicia after she's forced out of Florrick, Agos & Lockhart. The two become law partners as Florrick, Quinn & Associates. She went on to become a series regular onThe Good Fight. The Cynic: While far from heartless, she tells Alicia once that the key to working well with people is having low expectations of them, and says Alicia makes a poor bar attorney because she cares too much about her dozens of petty crime clients per day. Intergenerational Friendship: Like Cary, she hits it off quickly with Alicia despite the latter almost being old enough to be her mother. Suspiciously Similar Substitute: She essentially becomes the newToken Minorityand cynical counterpoint to Alicia with Kalinda's exit from the show.

characters.name: Jason Crouse
characters.description: A private investigator retained by Alicia and Lucca's law firm late in the series. He eventually begins a romantic relationship with Alicia. Beware the Nice Ones: A perfectly easygoing, charming guy, but he has a more violent side. He was once a lawyer himself but was disbarred for getting in a fistfight with a judge (who accuses him to Alicia of being a sociopath), and he's seen using a tire iron to get a scam victim's money back from theCon Artistwho stole it. Did Not Get the Girl:The series finale implies he chose to leave town rather than continue seeing Alicia and having to deal with herBig, Screwed-Up Family. Office Romance: He and Alicia are attracted from the first moment they lay eyes on one another and start sleeping together partway through the season (by this point Alicia and Peter have long since become aMarriage of Convenience). She insists they're justFriends with Benefitsand realizes she's fine after catching him with another woman on the side once, but it's strongly implied their feelings are stronger than either wants to admit. Suspiciously Similar Substitute: He essentially serves as aGender Flipof Kalinda for the final season: a dangerously competent PI with an unsavory butMysterious Past.

characters.name: Ruth Eastman
characters.description: A political strategist hired by Peter to manage his abortive presidential run, causing a rift between himself and Eli and a rivalry between the two of them. Beware the Nice Ones: She acts like a homey old Midwestern auntie, but she has a ton of experience reading the national opinion polls and maneuvering her candidate to take advantage. She even correctly predicts thatHillary Clintonwould pick a senator, not a governor, for her running mate, which happened after the show wrapped. Put on a Bus: She leaves the series in the mid-season finale "Tracks" following Peter's humiliating fourth-place finish in the Iowa Caucuses. She went on to appear in four episodes ofThe Good Fight. The Rival: To Eli, for Peter's affections. Peter hires her because she has experience running national campaigns, whereas Eli's experience is limited to Illinois, but Eli is understandably very miffed and initiallyquits in protest, then gets Peter to hire him back and starts trying to sabotage her and get Peter to take him back. Shipping Torpedo: In order to stop theOffice Romancebetween Alicia and Jason Crouse from imperiling Peter's presidential prospects, Ruth makes a good stab at breaking them up by persuading Peter's millionaire supporter Courtney Paige to hire him away to California for two months during Peter's attempted presidential run.

characters.name: Monica Timmons
characters.description: A young Loyola University graduate who interviews at Lockhart, Agos & Lee. Later becomes a minorrecurreronThe Good Fight. Commonality Connection:Invokedby Diane, who tries to pair her up with Lucca Quinn basically becausethey're both women of color. This induces eyerolls from them both: they don't dislike working together, they just find it patronizing that they're expected to naturally gravitate to each other. Passed-Over Promotion: She's initially passed over in hiring in favor of three white male Georgetown grads (Diane wanted to hire her but was outvoted), and retaliates byposting the video she took of the interview on the Internet to embarrass the firmand, as we find out later, filing an EEOC complaint. The Runner-Up Takes It All: Following the interview incident, she collaborates with the firm on a Chumhum case and impresses them, and then is able to squeeze the partners for very generous employment terms when the associates that were hired in her place jump shipen masseto Louis Canning and they need manpower in a hurry for a major case. To top it off, Cary is able to leverage the EEOC complaint she filed about her interview experience to finally force Howard out.
